hits.context: (1) Distinct Scope and Granularity. The core contribution of HybridKV is not merely an implementation tweak, but the discovery and utilization of attention head heterogeneity within Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs). We observed that attention heads in MLLMs exhibit distinct behaviors (static vs. dynamic) that are critical for multimodal understanding. TailorKV is designed for standard LLMs and operates at a coarser layer granularity, applying a uniform strategy (static quantization vs. dynamic retrieval) across all heads in a layer. To leverage this insight, we propose a novel set of algorithms introduced in Section 3, including head classification, top-down budget allocation, and head-specific compression strategies. These are designed to handle the complexity of multimodal inputs at the head level, a dimension that TailorKV does not explore. Therefore, our work addresses a new problem space (MLLM attention heterogeneity) with a finer-grained conceptual solution. We demonstrate performance comparisons between TailorKV and HybridKV in the response to W3.1 below.

hits.context: Core Contributions of Our Work Novel Inference System: We propose FloE, an on-the-fly MoE inference system designed for memory-constrained GPUs, leveraging untapped redundancy in sparsely activated experts to enhance performance. Effective Compression Scheme: FloE introduces new hybrid compression techniques to reduce the data movement load of expert parameter matrices, combined with low-cost sparse prediction, achieving significant inference acceleration on resource-constrained devices. Efficient System Optimization: We introduce an efficient sparse kernel and a compact asynchronous transfer mechanism from DRAM to VRAM, boosting system-wide efficiency. Extensive Experimental Evaluation: FloE achieves 9.3× parameter compression per expert in Mixtral-8×7B, enabling deployment on a GPU with only 11GB VRAM and reducing the memory footprint by up to 8.5×. It delivers a 48.7× inference speedup compared to DeepSpeed-MII on a single GeForce RTX 3090, with only a 4.4%–7.6% average performance degradation. Updates on Experiments and Discussions

hits.context: Core Contributions of Our Work Novel Discovery and Theoretical Potential: To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to explore loosely speculative decoding in the visual domain. We find that generation qualtiy is governed by sparse yet critical visual-relevant anchors and provide a rigorous theoretical analysis. Lightweight Framework: By employing a pinpoint and lightweight visual-relevant token identification and loose verification scheme, augmented by a position-shift tolerant mechanism, LVSPEC effectively shatters the rigid exact-match barrier in a training-free manner. Extensive Experimental Results: Comprehensive evaluations across four video understanding benchmarks show that LVSPEC is both high-fidelity and rapid. Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design Perspective: We move beyond isolated algorithmic improvements by analyzing how specific software optimizations interact with hardware constraints across the entire pipeline. Forward-Looking Empirical Insights: We propose visionary research directions, such as hybrid KV cache compression and relaxed speculative decoding, which are empirically grounded through visionary proofs-of-concept.
